design: docs/mechanics/LEGENDARY_HOMES.md section 4 (the cave kit), K1, K2 and K3; the owner's decisions of 2026-10-12 (Koraidon and Miraidon are post-Champion area bosses; Dialga goes to K5; Tapu Fini is a repeatable chamber spawn at K4; the boss respawn rule as proposed; rarity targets as proposed)
not_built: The kit supports the chamber features none, columns and crystal; a `pool` feature is refused by the generator until its water has a spawn-block policy entry (K4, The Strait Grotto, therefore has a dry chamber: its Tapu Fini and Nihilego spawn from the Habitat Block's pool on the grounded floor, which is unmeasured for water-typed species, HB-1). A rare-spawn chamber may host a second ultra-rare beast (`occupant.co_occupants`, K4's Nihilego), which the generator and the audit check as an ultra-rare entry of the chamber pool. Passages are straight (no `turn`): a cave is one axis from its mouth to its chamber. Natural-style Habitat Blocks in the passages are not emitted; only activated blocks (HB-1 and RS-1 are unmeasured). Passages of a kitted cave are straight; only a natural cave winds (`bend`), and its walls carry ore (`dressing.vein_one_in`), its floor patches (`dressing.patch_one_in`) and its hall `knobs`

geometry.rules: A cave is entered at its `mouth.anchor` (the middle column of the mouth) from its `mouth.front` (tools/mines.py frame(): north means the player stands north and the passage runs +z; south runs -z; west runs +x; east runs -x; u runs across, +x on a north or south front and +z on a west or east one; d runs into the hill, d = 0 is the mouth line). The mouth floor y0 is the lower median of the heightmap's ground (tools/ground.py, rounded) over row d = -1, u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1, where hw is the first passage's half width. Rows, in order: d = 0 the mouth (floor y0; timber posts at u = +-(hw+1) from y0+1 to y0+H and a beam of timber over u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1 at y0+H+1, H the first passage's height; one hanging lantern under the beam at u = 0); then the `passages` one after another, the first an `incline` of `length` = drop rows d = 1 .. drop, row d with floor top ft = y0 - d + 1 (a stair block facing the mouth's side, as the mining caves), the later ones level `drift` or `crawl` rows at yh = y0 - drop; then the `antechamber` if any (a room of half width `half_width`, `length` rows, `height`), then, if the cave has a gate, the door row (one row, half width door_half_width, height door_height, filled with barrier blocks over its whole cross-section) and `link_rows` rows of drift at half width door_half_width; then the oval `chamber`: centred on u = 0 at row dc = (its first row) + rz, a cell (u, d) is inside when u*u*rz*rz + (d-dc)^2*rx*rx <= rx*rx*rz*rz, air from yh+1 to yh+h over a floor at yh. Every row of a passage, link or room is air from its floor top + 1 to its floor top + height over u = -hw .. hw (the room's half width); an incline row whose least ground over u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1 is under its air top + 1 + cover_min.passage is an open cutting (air up to the higher of the ground and the air top, plus clear_above), every other row, and every room, must be a tunnel: ground over its air top >= the cover_min of its kind (passage 3, room 4). At most max_cutting_rows rows are cuttings. Shell: every non-air cell in the same column hull that lies within `margin` (passage 2, room 3, cutting 1) in x and z of an air column, from the lowest air cell minus the margin to the highest air cell plus the margin, is the cave's shell block, but only at or under ground - 1 (at or under ground next to a cutting). Wherever an air column's floor is more than one block over the ground, the cells from ground + 1 up to the floor (under a stair, under a floor, under a mouth post) are `fill` of the shell block, at most max_fill deep; the mouth's posts stand on such fill the same way. Lanterns stand on posts (a spruce fence block with a standing lantern on it, never a light block): on every row d of a level passage with (d - the passage's first row) % lantern_every == lantern_every // 2, alternately on the left and right wall column (u = -hw first, then +hw, counting across the whole cave), on the antechamber's two end corners (u = +-(half_width - 1) at its last row minus one), and four in the chamber at u = +-round(0.6 rx), d = dc +- round(0.55 rz). A chamber feature `columns` puts two full-height columns (the cave's column block) at u = +-round(0.5 rx), d = dc; `crystal` stands amethyst clusters (facing up) on the floor at the chamber cells the hash h32(seed, sid(cave id), u, d) orders first (tools/mines.py's mix; ties by (u, d)), `crystal_count` of them, skipping lantern posts and any cell with (u/rx)^2 + ((d-dc)/rz)^2 under 0.16. Rounding is Python's round(). The Habitat Block of a part replaces the floor cell at that part's centre (the chamber's centre; the antechamber's middle). NATURAL CAVES (`mode` "natural"; the owner, 2026-10-12: 'we need caves on Northlight, Long Isle and Sunset. They don't have to go anywhere or have a reward; just a cave would seem natural'). A natural cave has no gate, occupant, antechamber, Habitat Block, reward or keeper, and it writes no timber frame, no fence post, no lantern and no column: its mouth is the rock's own opening (no posts, no beam, no hanging lantern; the mouth-floor, apron, cutting and cover rules above are unchanged) and it is dark by design (lanterns are never written). Its later passages may WIND: a passage with an integer `bend` b (|b| no more than its length, a width of at least 3) puts its row i (0-based, of n rows) on the lateral offset c = c0 + floor((2*b*(i+1) + n) / (2*n)), that is b*(i+1)/n rounded half up, where c0 is the sum of the bends of the passages before it (0 for the mouth and the incline); its air is u = c - hw .. c + hw and the incline does not bend. The chamber is centred on u = uc, the sum of every bend, and a cell (u, d) is inside when (u-uc)^2*rz^2 + (d-dc)^2*rx^2 <= rx^2*rz^2; the shell, floor, fill, cover and cutting rules are otherwise as above, applied to the offset rows. A natural chamber's feature is `none` or `knobs`: `knobs` stands the palette's `knob` block on the floor (yh+1) at the `knob_count` chamber cells the same hash orders first as for `crystal` (u counted across the whole cave, the skip rule (u-uc)^2/rx^2 + (d-dc)^2/rz^2 under 0.16 likewise). DRESSING, once the shell and the knobs are written: every cell of the shell role (not a fill cell) that has an air cell among its six neighbours and whose h32(seed, sid(cave id), x, y, z) is a multiple of the cave's dressing.vein_one_in becomes the palette's `vein` block; every cell of the floor role (the mouth row, the level rows and the chamber, never a stair) whose h32(seed, sid(cave id), x, z, 7) is a multiple of dressing.patch_one_in becomes the palette's `patch` block. A natural cave's palette is shell, floor, stair, vein, patch and knob. HILLSIDE MOUTH (natural caves only; `geometry.natural_mouth` holds its numbers; the retired cutting rules above apply to a natural cave only as its `legacy`, see RESTORE). A natural cave opens no cutting: the sky is never opened over a row. The rows d = 0 .. drop (the mouth and the incline, u = -hw .. hw, never bent) are tunnel rows whatever the ground says, with no cover test, and their floor is a scree block (the cell's pick from the list `hillside.scree`: the entry h32(seed, sid, x, z, 3) mod the list's length), never a stair or a patch, and their shell is a cutting's (margin cutting, written up to the ground, not ground - 1) though their air is never opened. Let T(e) be row e's air top, floor top + height (floor top y0 on row 0 and y0 - e + 1 below). LID: over each air column of those rows the cells T+1 .. T+lid; a lid cell at or under the ground is the ground (or the shell) and stays, one above the ground is written (see MOUND). ARCH: on the rows d < arch_rows the two upper corner cells (u = +-hw, y = T) are rock (the rubble pick below) and not air. MOUND: for every column (u, d) outside the entry corridor (|u| <= hw and d < 0), let k be max(max(0, |u| - hw), dist), dist being 0 for 0 <= d <= drop, -d for d < 0 and d - drop above it (a column with k over natural_mouth.reach gets nothing), and let M be the maximum over the rows e = 0 .. drop of T(e) + lid - slope * max(max(0, |u| - hw), |d - e|), less h32(seed, sid, x, z, 9) mod 2 when k >= 2; where M is over the ground the cells ground + 1 .. M that the cave does not already write are written: rock below the top (the entry h32(seed, sid, x, y, z, 11) mod the length of the list `hillside.rubble`), and at the top cell the cave's `terrain.surface` block, unless the column is in the face (d <= 1 and |u| <= hw + face_extra) or h32(seed, sid, x, z, 13) mod speckle_one_in = 0, when the top cell is rock too. APRON: on -apron_reach <= d <= -1 and |u| <= hw the cell at y = ground becomes a scree block (the pick h32(seed, sid, x, z, 5)) when h32(seed, sid, x, z, 6) mod 100 < 100 - 20 * (-d - 1). VINES (`hillside.vine` true): at u = -hw .. hw, d = -1 and y = T(0)+1 .. T(0)+lid, a `minecraft:vine` with one face set, the side of the lid cell behind it (east on a west front, west on an east front, south on a north front, north on a south front), wherever the vine's cell is above the ground and the lid cell behind it is written. SITING: the least ground over u = -hw .. hw at row d = drop is at least rise_min above y0 (the incline enters a slope). The palette of a natural cave is shell, floor, vein, patch and knob (no stair); the hillside lists, the terrain blocks and the vine flag are the cave's `hillside` and `terrain`. No block it writes is cut, smooth, polished, chiselled, brick, a stair, a slab, a wall, a fence, timber or a lantern. RESTORE: a natural cave's `legacy` is the frozen record (mouth, passages, chamber) of the mouth the retired rules built and the world still holds; the pack's function restore_<id> puts every column that retired cave wrote to (its cells computed by the rules above WITHOUT this paragraph, a cutting where the cover test says so and a stair on the incline) back to terrain over the y range it wrote: `terrain.deep` from the lowest cell to ground - 3, `terrain.under` from ground - 2 to ground - 1, `terrain.surface` at the ground, air above it to the highest cell; the heightmap's rounded ground, never a world. build_<id> calls it first, so a re-run restores and builds again to the same world, and a world that never held the retired cave only has its own terrain written over itself.

natural_mouth.why: The owner, 2026-10-12, after seeing a mouth in game: "a cut stone trench in open meadow with a timber frame ... I hate the cave look, it feels out of place"; for the three natural caves: "Natural hillside mouths": an organic opening in a slope, no trench, no frame, no cut stone. The islands' ground is gentle (the heightmap rises about 0.3 a block into the hills the three caves stand in, and the steepest faces a 3-block scan of the N1 and N2 rings found, 2026-10-12, still left 5 and 4 incline rows without cover against today's 7 and 7), so a hillside is grown more than found: the rock the opening needs is added over and beside it as a mound of the hill's own surface block with rock showing at the face, and the surface above the rest of the cave is left as terrain. lid is the rock thickness over the mouth and incline air; slope the mound's fall per block; reach how far out from the lid it runs; arch_rows how many rows lose their upper corner cells; apron_reach how far the scree runs out in front; rise_min the least rise of the ground over the incline for a mouth to count as in a slope; speckle_one_in how often a mound's top is rock and not the surface block; face_extra how far beyond the opening's half width the face rows show rock.

keep_clear.why: tools/mining_caves.py Clearance, reused as it stands (see its docstring): every written column keeps these distances from the town footprints, the routed legs and route paths, the routes' spawn-corridor boxes, every x/z another data file authors (this file, the exempt Habitat Block ids and the exempt files below skipped), every earthwork and placed template, every other built pack's writes, painted water and the water export's changed columns; a surface column keeps tree_reach from a painted tree. authored_clearance is 32 here (12 for the mining caves): a cave is a place, not a gallery. `report` also lists everything within report_radius so the owner can see what is near

authored_exempt.ids: computed by tools/caves.py: every Habitat Block id this file authors (habitat[].id of each cave) is skipped by id in tools/southern_residents.py authored_points, because it stands inside the cave it belongs to; every other Habitat Block in data/habitat_blocks.json stays a keep-clear point

files.world_probes.json: this tool's own presence probes (places.caves in data/world_probes.json) are positions inside the caves

gate.why: legendaries.py's partition pattern (tools/legendaries.py files(): near / open / close): the door opens while a flagged player stands in the antechamber and closes when none does and nobody stands in the door, link or chamber. The driver runs only while somebody is within `reach` of the chamber centre, so whoever trips it holds the chunks it writes

caves.name: Hoarfrost Hollow
caves.role: a natural cave on the south Pine Isle, away from Northlight: nowhere to go and nothing to take
caves.reading: A rock-split opening in a snow-covered spruce hillside, scree running out in front of it: the rock sweats frost, the floor is ice in patches and the little hall at the end of the twisting way has blue ice standing in it like teeth. Nothing lives here but the dark.

light.why: a natural cave is left dark: the night is fightorflight's and a dark cave is the right kind of danger (docs/STATE.md); no lantern is ever written

mouth.sited_by: tools/caves.py author (the first sitting) then moved [6714, 1350] -> [6724, 1348] on 2026-10-12 for the hillside mouth: the best of a 2-block grid within 16 blocks that passes every geometry and keep-clear rule (the mound would otherwise stand within tree_reach of painted trees); smallest mound plus twice the move. A 3-block scan of the whole ring found no face that avoids a built mouth (the best left 4 or 5 incline rows without cover), so the mound grows the slope geometry.natural_mouth needs

legacy.why: the first natural mouth, applied in staging 2026-10-12: an incline opened to the sky as a stone-lined cutting (6 or 7 rows) in open meadow; the owner: "I hate the cave look, it feels out of place". It is taken down first (RESTORE in geometry.rules) and the hillside mouth built; frozen so the demolition does not move when the record does.

hillside.why: bare frost-split stone under the snow cap: grey cobble and andesite, no moss, no vines
